newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: MUGABE MAN WINS ZIMBABWE MAYORAL ELECTION.
newsitem.headline: MUGABE MAN WINS ZIMBABWE MAYORAL ELECTION.

text.p: President Robert Mugabe's ruling ZANU-PF party won the executive mayoral election in Zimbabwe's town of Chitungwiza at the weekend, polling officials said on Monday.

But its opponent in the race, independent candidate Fidelis Mhashu who polled 3,374 votes to ZANU-PF's Andrew Jiri who polled 4,435, rejected the result, saying he would challenge it in court on grounds the electoral system was flawed.
Some 12 percent of 70,000 registered voters took part in the two-day poll in Chitungwiza, the southern African country's third most populous town with over one million residents.
Mhashu was expelled from the ruling party after opting to stand as an independent in defiance of Jiri's selection as the official ZANU-PF representative.
